approach: Check whether three forces at the given fixed angles can ever sum to zero for any positive magnitudes, by testing whether their directions surround the origin.

steps.text: Place F₁ along 0°. F₂ is 30° from F₁, so place it at 30°. F₃ is 120° from F₁, and this angle alone does not say on which side, so try F₃ at 120° or at −120°.
Three concurrent forces can balance to zero only if no gap between consecutive directions, going around the full circle, exceeds 180°.
For F₃ at 120°, the directions are 0°, 30°, 120°; the gaps between them are 30°, 90°, and 240°, and the 240° gap exceeds 180°, so equilibrium is impossible.
For F₃ at −120° (same as 240°), the directions are 0°, 30°, 240°; the gaps are 30°, 210°, and 120°, and the 210° gap also exceeds 180°, so equilibrium is impossible here too.

Both possible placements fail, so the assertion is true: the forces cannot be in equilibrium. The reason describes this as one pairwise angle between two of the forces exceeding 180°, but a pairwise angle between two forces is always taken between 0° and 180° by convention and never exceeds it, so the reason's stated criterion is false.

final_answer.value: (c) The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.

common_mistakes.text: Accepting the reason's claim that one pairwise angle must exceed 180° as the correct explanation, even though such an angle is always kept within 0° to 180°, leads to picking option (a) instead of (c).
